title: Companies Act, 2013 — Section 378ZK (Loan, etc., to Members)

content.overview: Section 378ZK permits the Board, subject to the company's articles, to provide financial assistance to Members through (a) a credit facility connected with the Producer Company's business for no more than six months, or (b) loans and advances secured as specified in the articles and repayable after more than three months but within seven years. A loan or advance to a director or the director's relative requires approval by Members in general meeting.
content.glance: Member financial assistance is limited to the credit, loan and advance routes in section 378ZK, subject to the articles, term limits, specified security and general-meeting approval for loans/advances to directors or their relatives.
content.study: Companies Act, 2013 — Section 378ZK (Loan, etc., to Members). Subject to the company's articles, the Board may provide financial assistance to Members through a credit facility connected with the Producer Company's business for a period not exceeding six months, or loans and advances against security specified in the articles, repayable after more than three months but not more than seven years from disbursement. The section's proviso requires approval by Members in general meeting before any loan or advance is granted to a director or the director's relative. Legal verification remains open.

sections.heading: Credit facility
sections.body: The Board may provide a credit facility to a Member in connection with the Producer Company's business for a period not exceeding six months, subject to the provisions made in the articles.

sections.heading: Loans and advances
sections.body: The Board may provide loans and advances to a Member against security specified in the articles, repayable within a period exceeding three months but not exceeding seven years from the date of disbursement.

sections.heading: Director or relative
sections.body: Any loan or advance to a director or the director's relative may be granted only after approval by Members in general meeting.

examples.title: Reviewing a proposed Member loan
examples.body: Check that the recipient is a Member, identify whether the assistance is a credit facility or a loan/advance, apply the relevant duration and security conditions, and verify general-meeting approval if the recipient is a director or the director's relative.

hypotheticals.question: The Board proposes a seven-year loan to a Member who is also a director. What section 378ZK conditions must be checked?
hypotheticals.analysis: Verify the loan is against security specified in the articles and that the repayment term does not exceed seven years or fall outside the stated range. Because the recipient is a director, the proviso requires approval by Members in general meeting before the loan or advance is granted.

distinctions.title: Credit facility and loan/advance
distinctions.left: A credit facility must be connected with the Producer Company's business and may not exceed six months.
distinctions.right: A loan or advance must be secured as specified in the articles and repaid after more than three months but within seven years.

rows.right: Exceeding three months and not exceeding seven years

misconceptions.trap: Treating the six-month credit-facility period as the term for all loans and advances.
misconceptions.correction: Apply the separate repayment period stated for loans and advances.

misconceptions.trap: Assuming the Board may grant a loan or advance to a director or relative without Member approval.
misconceptions.correction: The proviso requires approval by Members in general meeting before the loan or advance is granted.

misconceptions.trap: Ignoring the security specified in the articles for loans and advances.
misconceptions.correction: Check the company's articles for the security condition stated in section 378ZK.

questionsAndAnswers.question: What does section 378zk do?
questionsAndAnswers.answer: The Board may provide financial assistance to Members, in the form of credit, loans or advances, subject to the articles and the limits the section imposes.
